answer: The network caps how much any single account can take per epoch, so even a cleverly large farm cannot monopolize one epoch's rewards — the surplus is spread across many passing identities. This matters because the cost of running many aliases grows faster than the influence they can exert, making the attack economically self-defeating. The practical upshot is that honesty is the only strategy that scales — a farm that tries to game the system pays for each identity it adds. Consider a dawn as the anchor of the cost.
